title: Profiling memory with Chrome DevTools and heap snapshots
hook: Chrome DevTools Memory panel shows what objects live on the heap, who retains them, and whether memory grows without bound — the production-debugging skill for browser leaks and allocation regressions.

blocks.text: **Heap snapshot**: point-in-time graph of all JS objects. **Comparison**: diff two snapshots after repeating suspect action — shows what grew. **Allocation timeline**: record allocations over time, stack traces to constructor site. **Retainers view**: path from object to GC root explaining why not collected.

blocks.text: Without profiling you guess — add random gc() calls. Senior engineers reproduce leak (open/close modal 20x), diff snapshots, find `(closure)` retaining Detached HTMLElement, fix missing teardown. Same workflow for fetch response caches in SPAs.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Single snapshot without baseline. Not forcing GC before compare (minor). Ignoring retained size vs shallow size.

blocks.text: Report: action reproduced, delta count, retainer path screenshot, fix PR. Allocation instrumentation links to stack — find `new Array` in hot path. Compare with Lighthouse not sufficient for leaks — need heap diff.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Never used heap snapshot. Confuses CPU profiler with memory. Cannot read retainer path.

interviewTakeaways: Retainers explain why object not GC'd.
Detached DOM visible in snapshot filter.
60s: Heap snapshot = object graph. Diff after repeat action. Retainers walk to root. Node --inspect same. Fix reference not gc().
